root_cause.text: The `skb_gro_receive_list()` function in `net/core/gro.c` calls `skb_pull()` to adjust the socket buffer offset without first verifying that the required header data resides in the linear area via `pskb_may_pull()`.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff adds a check `if (!pskb_may_pull(skb, skb_gro_offset(skb)))` to `skb_gro_receive_list()` in `net/core/gro.c` to prevent a kernel panic (`BUG_ON(skb->len < skb->data_len)`) in `__skb_pull()` when processing packets with zero headlen (e.g., from `napi_gro_frags()`).

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a safety check to ensure sufficient linear data is present in the skb before performing GRO list reception.
intent_record.what: Added a conditional check using pskb_may_pull to verify the skb has sufficient linear data up to skb_gro_offset, setting the flush flag and returning -ENOMEM on failure.
intent_record.how: Prevents potential out-of-bounds memory access during GRO list processing by ensuring the packet header data is accessible in the linear buffer.
